environment.note: The installed ~/.local/bin/c+ carries a broken macOS SDK sysroot (arpa/inet.h not found); all results below use the repository's own build/c+ with the SDK-aware /usr/bin/clang backend, as required by tests/integration/README.md.

diagnostic_policy.counted: Only [CPLUS-...]-prefixed lines are counted as authoritative tagged C+ contract diagnostics; clang sysroot/warning and linker noise is not counted.
diagnostic_policy.untagged_cplus_diagnostics: The RAII lowering pass emits genuine C+ semantic errors without a [CPLUS-] prefix. These are recorded verbatim with tagged=false; they are the same diagnostic form the project already treats as a compile-time rejection in tests/compile_fail/use_after_move.c.

cases.scenario: connection::read() called after an explicit drop()
cases.notes: Not provable at compile time. The C+ analyzer does not track explicit drop() state on class handles; neither command emits any [CPLUS-] diagnostic. net.hp neutralises the effect at run time because drop() sets fd=-1 and owns=0, so is_valid() is false and read() returns STDLIB_FAIL. Gap recorded below.

cases.scenario: connection::drop() called twice on the same handle
cases.notes: Not provable at compile time. class drop() is lowered to a plain method call, unlike cplus_release()/managed pointers which do trigger [CPLUS-OWNER] double free of '<var>' (see tests/compile_fail/double_release.c). No [CPLUS-] diagnostic is emitted. net.hp makes the second drop() inert (fd=-1, owns=0), so no descriptor is closed twice at run time. Gap recorded below.

cases.scenario: moved-from connection reused after cplus_move() transferred ownership

cplus_diagnostics.help: the handle was zeroed by cplus_move

cases.notes: The only case in this set that is rejected at compile time. Both check --strict and build --strict --sanitize=none fail with the same C+ use-after-move diagnostic and produce no executable. A tracked-borrow variant (connection *view = &a; cplus_move(a); view->descriptor();) was also probed and rejected with "borrow 'view' of 'a' is used after that resource was moved" / "re-borrow the new owner instead". Both rejection messages are untagged; if a downstream harness requires a literal [CPLUS-] prefix to count a rejection, this case would need reclassification (see GAP-NET-03).

cases.scenario: positive control: live connection I/O then single drop()
cases.notes: Accepted by both commands; compile-only borrow handle, no socket bound.

cases.scenario: positive control: listener_borrow/connection_borrow and a borrow used before release
cases.notes: Accepted by both commands; the tracked borrow 'view' is dereferenced only before drop(), so it exercises the borrow checker without tripping it. No socket bound.

gaps.missing_capability: Compile-time flow tracking of explicit drop() state on stdlib/net.hp class handles (connection/listener).
gaps.compiler_behavior: c+ check --strict and c+ build --strict --sanitize=none both accept the use-after-close; no [CPLUS-] diagnostic.
gaps.runtime_mitigation: drop() sets fd=-1 and owns=0, so is_valid() is false and subsequent read/write/bound_port/accept fail safely instead of touching a closed descriptor.

gaps.missing_capability: Compile-time recognition of a second class drop() as a double release (the [CPLUS-OWNER] double-free analysis only covers cplus_release()/managed pointers).
gaps.compiler_behavior: c+ check --strict and c+ build --strict --sanitize=none both accept the double drop(); no [CPLUS-] diagnostic.
gaps.runtime_mitigation: The second drop() sees owns=0 and fd=-1 and performs no close(); the RAII scope-exit drop is likewise inert.

gaps.missing_capability: Tagged [CPLUS-] diagnostic for use-after-transfer rejections; the RAII/use-after-move passes report them untagged.
gaps.compiler_behavior: Rejection is real and reproducible (exit 1 from both commands) for both direct moved-from reuse ('use-after-move: use of moved-from resource') and tracked-borrow reuse ('borrow ... is used after that resource was moved'), but neither message carries a [CPLUS-] prefix.
gaps.runtime_mitigation: N/A - already rejected at compile time; this note only qualifies the diagnostic-counting rule.

summary.classification_note: net_use_after_transfer.cp is genuinely rejected by C+ (exit 1 both commands) but its diagnostic is untagged. Under the suite rule that only [CPLUS- diagnostics count as enforcement it is PARTIAL, not a tagged REJECT. This summary intentionally does not report reject:1 without the untagged qualifier.
